brief:
The war in Gaza has created unprecedented divisions within American politics, challenging long-standing bipartisan support for Israeli military operations. The Quincy Institute examined how the conflict has reshaped voter priorities and party coalitions across the country.

Traditional consensus on US Middle East policy has fractured along generational and ideological lines, with younger voters and progressive Democrats increasingly critical of American support for Israel's military campaign. The shift reflects broader debates over humanitarian concerns, civilian casualties, and the US role in regional conflicts that cut across typical party boundaries.
title: Gaza conflict fractures US political consensus on Middle East
